entries.title: Little Samson

entries.title: Mega Man
entries.summary: Capcom's 1987 action platformer directed by Akira Kitamura: Mega Man takes on Dr. Wily's six Robot Masters (Cut, Guts, Ice, Bomb, Fire, Elec), then Wily's fortress.
entries.why_it_matters: The start of the Mega Man series and Capcom's first game made specifically for home consoles. It set the choose-your-stage, steal-the-weapon formula.
entries.gameplay_notes: Six stages in any order; each Robot Master is weak to another's weapon. The Magnet Beam from Elec Man's stage makes platforms. Wily's fortress is four linked stages plus a boss rematch gauntlet, with no ammo refill between them. The score counter was dropped in later games.

difficulty.reason: Widely seen as very difficult; USGamer called it 'the introduction of Nintendo Hard'.

entries.title: Mega Man 2

entries.gameplay_notes: Adds Energy Tanks, passwords and three platform items. Boss weaknesses reward choosing the stage order carefully. The Wily rematches are a teleporter room. Cleared stages can't be revisited, and there is no score.

entries.title: Metroid
entries.summary: Nintendo R&D1 and Intelligent Systems' 1986 exploration action game: bounty hunter Samus Aran infiltrates planet Zebes to destroy Mother Brain and the stolen Metroids.
entries.why_it_matters: Pioneered the Metroidvania genre. The reveal that Samus is a woman made it one of the first games with a female protagonist, and its time-based endings helped make it an early speedrunning favourite.
entries.gameplay_notes: Non-linear caverns opened up by power-ups: Morph Ball, bombs, Screw Attack, Ice Beam, missiles. Defeat Kraid and Ridley to open the way to Mother Brain. There are five endings based on completion time. 24-character passwords (including the famous 'NARPAS SWORD' cheat).

difficulty.reason: A large, open-ended world with passwords instead of saves.

entries.title: Ninja Crusaders
entries.summary: NMK's side-scrolling action game from Sammy: ninjas Talon and Blade fight an alien invasion that has overrun Japan.

entries.title: Ninja Gaiden
entries.summary: Tecmo's 1988 ninja action platformer: Ryu Hayabusa goes to America to avenge his father and stop the Jaquio from awakening a demon.
entries.why_it_matters: Known for its elaborate story told through anime-style cinematic cutscenes. One of the most acclaimed NES games, and famous for its difficulty.
entries.gameplay_notes: Six Acts across 20 levels. Wall-jumping, Dragon Sword attacks, and sub-weapons (shuriken, windmill star, fire wheel, jump & slash) powered by spiritual strength. Bosses are the Malice Four. Unlimited continues restart the current level.

difficulty.reason: Criticised for its high difficulty, particularly in the later levels.

entries.title: Ninja Gaiden II: The Dark Sword of Chaos
entries.summary: Tecmo's 1990 sequel: Ryu stops the emperor Ashtar from opening the Gate of Darkness with the Dark Sword of Chaos.
entries.why_it_matters: Improved visuals and controls over the original while keeping its difficulty.
entries.gameplay_notes: Ryu can now climb up and down walls and use sub-weapons while clinging. New Fire Dragon Balls. Scrolls raise maximum ninja power. Acts end with bosses; continues restart the level.

difficulty.reason: Reviewers noted it keeps the series' high difficulty.

entries.title: Ninja Gaiden III: The Ancient Ship of Doom
entries.summary: Tecmo's 1991 entry designed by Masato Kato and set between the first two games: Ryu, framed for Irene Lew's murder, uncovers Foster and Clancy's bio-noid plot.
entries.gameplay_notes: Adds overhead pipe hanging, sword power-ups and the Vacuum Wave Art. More sci-fi enemies.

difficulty.reason: The US version doubles damage taken compared with Japan and limits you to five continues.

entries.title: Ninja Kid
entries.summary: Tose's action game from Bandai, a retitled GeGeGe no Kitarō game with all Kitaro references removed: complete side-scrolling missions picked from an overhead map.
entries.why_it_matters: The Japanese original was the eighth best-selling Famicom game of 1986, at 1.25 million copies.
entries.gameplay_notes: The shape of each map arch hints at the mission type. After each mission, one of two doors returns you to the map and the other leads to a mini-boss tower; an owl item shows which is which. Collect a scroll to open the map's boss fortress. Whistles summon a familiar during boss fights.

entries.title: Nintendo World Cup
entries.summary: Technōs Japan's Kunio-kun soccer game, localised by Nintendo: rough six-a-side street soccer with no offsides, no fouls and super shots.
entries.gameplay_notes: Tackle opponents until they're knocked out for the half. Up to five super shots per half, which differ by team. Fields include sand, ice and dirt. Tournament mode with 13 teams, and VS mode for up to four players with the Four Score or Satellite.

entries.title: Nobunaga's Ambition
entries.summary: Koei's Sengoku-era strategy game, the first Nobunaga's Ambition released in English: unify Japan as Oda Nobunaga or a rival daimyo.
entries.gameplay_notes: Four scenarios (1560–1582). Seasonal turns covering taxes, rice, flood control, cultivation, merchants, ninja, spies, marriages and pacts, with peasant loyalty always at risk. Battles are fought day by day.
